summary: Square steel skeletal tower on Racine's north breakwater: the 1901 North Pierhead Light, moved here in 1924, dark since 1987, now a closed city-owned landmark.

lens.note: Fourth-order lens moved from the Racine Harbor Lighthouse into the 1901 tower (LighthouseFriends).

structures.type: square steel skeletal, with lantern and gallery, painted red
structures.note: 46 ft (14 m) per Rowlett. First light 23 November 1901 (LighthouseFriends) or 23 November 1902 (Pepper). Moved from the north pier to the south pier in 1912 and to the breakwater in 1924.

staffing.note: Breakwater light controlled remotely after telephone and control cable was laid in 1933 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Site and tower closed (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends). Floodlit at night. Visible across the harbor entrance from the viewing platform in Racine Harbor Park (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: City of Racine (owner and site manager per Rowlett and LighthouseFriends)
facts.keepers_quarters: The old Racine Harbor station was converted into a dwelling for the head keeper and his assistant from about 1902 (Pepper); the USLHS record gives the quarters as 1886, a date not matched by either other source.

events.note: Wooden pierhead beacon at the outer end of the north pier first exhibited its fixed red light on 5 September 1872 (LighthouseFriends; Pepper).
A conduit 288 feet long replaced the pierhead beacon; the beacon's light was discontinued (Light-House Board, 1894; LighthouseFriends dates the conduit light to 28 May 1894).
A sixth-order light was re-established on the north pier on 18 June 1896, with a fog bell (Light-House Board, 1896; Pepper).
Detached breakwater completed in November 1900; a temporary fixed red lantern was placed on its end (LighthouseFriends; Pepper gives 13 October 1900).
Steel tower erected at the end of the north pier; lighted 23 November 1901 (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett). Pepper gives 23 November 1902.
Fourth-order Fresnel lens from the Racine Harbor Lighthouse placed in the new tower (LighthouseFriends).

Tower moved from the north pier to the outer end of the south pier; showed a white flashing light from 29 May 1912 (LighthouseFriends). The Lighthouse Service Bulletin lists Racine Pierhead among lights changed from fixed to flashing, by acetylene.
November 1913: the steamer Nyanza, unloading coal at a Racine dock, was caught in a storm; her captain's account is quoted by LighthouseFriends.
Tower transferred from the south pier to the breakwater (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).
18,000 feet of telephone and control cable laid by the tender Hyacinth, allowing the breakwater light to be controlled remotely (LighthouseFriends).
Breakwater light discontinued; inactive since 1987, charted as a landmark (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends).
Coast Guard planned to remove the tower; a public outcry saved it (LighthouseFriends; Pepper).

corrections.why: No source supports 1831 for this site. The first light on this pier, the wooden pierhead beacon, was first exhibited on 5 September 1872 (LighthouseFriends; Pepper). The first Racine light on the bluff dates from 1838 and is a different structure.
Pepper gives a focal plane of 53 feet, which is 16.2 m. The record's 53.0 has the unit wrong.

Rowlett gives the quick-flashing green light, with its fog horn and USCG 7-20495, to Racine West Harbor Entrance, an active, privately maintained light. The North Breakwater's light was fixed red when lit and has been dark since 1987.
Rowlett gives USCG 7-20495 to the West Harbor Entrance light. The North Breakwater entry in Rowlett carries only ARLHS USA-682.

corrections.current: Racine West Harbor Entrance, Racine West Harbor Entrance Light 3
corrections.why: Both names belong to the active West Harbor Entrance light, which Rowlett lists separately, not to the North Breakwater tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1872 is the first light on this pier, the wooden pierhead beacon. 1901 is the steel tower built at the end of the north pier. Terry Pepper's 1902 first-light date and LighthouseFriends' and Rowlett's 1901 disagree; the story gives both.
1987 is the year the breakwater light was discontinued (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett; Pepper). Consistent across all three.

notes_for_editor: The USLHS place record (archives.uslhs.org/places/racine-north-breakwater, not cited in the story) lists a 1872 tower and a 4th-order lens installed in 1872, a 46 ft height above mean high water, keeper's quarters built 1886, and 'Active Aid to Navigation: No'. Pepper and LighthouseFriends say the first lens in 1872 was sixth order and that the fourth-order lens came in 1901, so the USLHS 1872 optic date is probably wrong; the record's Wikidata 1831 date has no support. The USLHS latitude and longitude ('42 73.40 / 87 77.20') are invalid minutes, and the roster tool's 43.2233, -88.2867 is a parsing artifact; the record's OSM point (42.734604, -87.772029) is plausible and was left alone. The record's QG light, fog horn and focal height of 53 m belong to the Racine West Harbor Entrance light and Pepper's 53 feet, not to this tower. Martin N. Knudsen: LighthouseFriends says head keeper 1899 to 1917, but the 1921 Bulletin printed a letter from a Martin Knudsen as keeper of the Racine Pierhead Light Station; the two are not reconciled. Edward W. Knudsen: LighthouseFriends lists him as head keeper 1917 to 1932, but the 1915 Bulletin report and later Bulletin indexes name an Edward W. Knudsen as keeper of the Racine Reef light, a separate light; the 1915 report's header reads 'EDWARD W. [OCR-damaged] KEEPER' and is read here as Knudsen (check the page image before relying on the surname); the 1912-1917 Bulletin index lists 'Knudsen, Edward, keeper Racine Reef light station, reports major storm 155'. Edward R. Knudson appears in a 1913 Bulletin item as keeper of Racine Reef. These may be the same man at two lights or different men; no source settles it, and the keeper roster is LighthouseFriends' list cited as a fact source. The LighthouseFriends keeper list covers the Racine harbor station as a whole, including the 1839 to 1865 keepers of the earlier harbor lights; it does not say which keeper tended the breakwater tower in each year. Pepper links a full keeper list compiled by Phyllis L. Tag, which was not read. The Light-House Board's 1893 and 1900 entries and the Commissioner's 1919 fog-signal lists were not used because the status of the North Breakwater entry in those lists could not be confirmed from the text. Wikipedia was not cited (lead only); the Racine County Eye 2017 article was not read in full. LighthouseFriends gives Racine Harbor light as 1866 and Pepper gives 1865; the story does not use either date.
